title: pkix-path: ~45 survivors left, led by the name-constraint intersection
description:
## Why

pkix-path's sweep found 100 survivors; roughly 45 remain after five rounds
of fixes. Grouped by what they are about.

## Clusters

**Name-constraint intersection in chain_walk.** The `subtree_within` calls
and `already_in_result`. This is RFC 5280 §6.1.4 (g) permitted/excluded
subtree intersection -- the machinery that makes a constraint on an
intermediate bind everything below it. Highest value of what is left:
a wrong intersection is a trust-scope defect, which is the class the
§4.2.1.10 and SMTP-DANE findings earlier in this sweep belonged to.

**§6.1.1 path length.** `>` to `>=` on the max-path-length comparison, and
the `max_chain_certs` arithmetic. Boundary cases, the same shape as the CRL
and OCSP freshness windows closed in pkix-revocation: inclusive at the
documented end, and nothing asserts which end.

**policy_graph (3).** RFC 5280 §6.1.3/§6.1.4 policy mapping and the
valid-policy tree.

**sha1_digest (3).** Verify-only, opt-in per the project stance. Pinning it
needs a known-answer vector, which is a two-line test against the RFC 3174
sample.

**serde_der.rs (11).** The DER serde shims. Same class as
pkix-revocation's `crl_reason_serde`, where a round-trip over every variant
with hand-written wire values killed all eleven -- that is the template.

**check_max_validity.** One comparison.

**NormalizedIter / DirStringBytes (5).** RFC 4518 string prep internals
feeding `names_match`. Behavioural, and `names_match` is security-relevant;
these want direct unit tests on the iterator rather than tests through DN
comparison.

**Public helpers with no in-crate caller.** `cert_is_ca`,
`tbs_certificate_der`. A crate-scoped sweep cannot reach them by
construction; consumers may cover them, and that needs checking per case
rather than assuming either way. `pkix-identity`'s
`dns_name_matches_pattern` was the same shape and did turn out to be
entirely untested.

## Method

Re-run to regenerate the list:

    cargo mutants -p pkix-path --all-features -j 4 --timeout-multiplier 4

Six mutants timed out on the first run; `--timeout-multiplier 4` is what
keeps a slow-but-correct test from being read as a hang.

## Found by

The pkix-path mutation sweep, 2026-11-27: 552 mutants, 100 missed.
notes:
## Fresh sweep, 2026-11-27

    556 mutants, 47 missed, 439 caught, 64 unviable, 6 timeouts

Down from 100 missed. The 6 timeouts are `DirStringBytes::next` and
`NormalizedIter::next` -- the RFC 4518 string-prep iterators. A timeout
means the mutation makes the suite hang rather than answer wrongly, so
those are detected; they are not coverage gaps.

Closed since: NcTypeMask's eight constraint bits and both union operators
(417509f1), the unevaluable-name-form rules in check_san_name_form and the
emailAddress guard in check_name_constraints (15eb83c8), and the option /
vec / option_vec serde helpers (ac430b2b).

## What is left, by cluster

**chain_walk, 6.** The name-constraint intersection. 4192/4193 and 4218 are
the two-way `subtree_within` dedup conjunctions, 4195 the
`!already_in_result`, and 3934/3959 two `==` comparisons. 4218 is the
fail-open one: it dedups EXCLUDED subtrees, and a one-way containment
treated as equality drops the broader exclusion, so names that should be
excluded are allowed. Wants a chain where two CAs exclude nested subtrees
(`sub.bad.example` then `bad.example`) and a leaf under the broader one.

**The RSA-PSS backend, ~10.** verify_rsa_pss (3), rsa_public_key (2),
pad_prehash (2), rfc4055_hash (1), and three `verify_signature -> Ok(())`
at lib.rs:781 and :811. The Ok(()) ones are the fail-open shape -- a
verifier that accepts everything. Known-answer vectors are the cheap way
in: RFC 4055 and the NIST PSS test vectors.

**validate_path / max_chain_certs, 4.** `>` to `>=` at 1680 and 1694, and
the arithmetic at 1822. Boundary cases, the shape already closed for the
CRL and OCSP freshness windows in pkix-revocation: assert the documented
end is inclusive.

**policy_graph, 3.** intersect_user_policy_set, apply_policy_mappings,
prune_above_deepest -> (). RFC 5280 §6.1.3/§6.1.4.

**Public helpers with no in-crate caller, 5.** cert_is_ca (2) and
tbs_certificate_der (3). A crate-scoped sweep cannot reach them by
construction; consumers may cover them, which needs checking per case.
pkix-identity's dns_name_matches_pattern was this shape and was entirely
untested.

**Display / source / eq / hash, 6.** lib.rs:230 `eq -> true`, :255 `hash`,
:307 and :571 `fmt -> Ok(())`, :313 and :650 `source -> None`. The pattern
is settled: enumerate the variants, assert non-empty and pairwise
distinct, the way pkix-revocation's display_tests does. `eq -> true` is the
one with teeth -- it is a trust-anchor or DN equality.

**ip_constraint_within, 1.** `==` to `!=` at 3152.

**NcTypeMask::RFC822's shift, 1.** `1 << 0` and `1 >> 0` are the same
number. Unkillable; noted in the module.
